items.q: Why is it so hard to keep weight off?
items.a: The brain treats weight loss as a threat: it **raises hunger** and **lowers metabolism**, and the drop looks **largely permanent**.

items.q: What is exercise actually good for in weight control?
items.a: It is weak for losing weight but **strong for maintenance**, offsetting the lower metabolism.

items.q: What best predicts health span as you age?
items.a: Your **muscle-to-fat ratio** heading into your late 60s and 70s.

items.q: How much of protein's label calories do you actually use?
items.a: About **70%**; the rest is lost as heat while **processing protein**.

items.q: Why does cooked celery give more calories than raw?
items.a: **Cooking and processing** make calories **easier to extract** from the same food.

items.q: What is the problem with obsessing over calorie counts?
items.a: It ignores **food quality**, so people pick a smaller number over a **more nutritious meal**.

items.q: What happens when your fat cells are full?
items.a: Fat **spills into the liver and muscles**, which is when **metabolic disease** starts.

items.q: Why do East and South Asians face risk at lower BMI?
items.a: They can **store less fat safely**, so they reach **diabetes risk at a lower weight**.

items.q: What simple diet rule does Giles Yeo suggest?
items.a: About **16% protein**, **double the fibre**, and **free sugars under 5%** of energy.
